name: Borde: in dimensions >= 3 causally compact topology-changing spacetimes cannot satisfy Einstein's equation with a reasonable source (gr-qc/9406053 abstract; Sec. V Theorem 3)

source.located: A. Borde, 'Topology change in classical general relativity', arXiv:gr-qc/9406053v1, 30 Jun 1994. The abstract (p.1) holds the sentence. Sec. II.A defines the interpolating spacetime (smooth Lorentz metric, S1 and S2 spacelike, T compact and timelike, time-oriented). Sec. III.B defines causal compactness. Sec. V gives Theorem 3 with assumptions (i) and (ii), their discussion V.A-B, and the proof V.C with Lemma A and focusing eq. (1). Sec. VI says which T_ab give (ii). Sec. IX.B gives the escapes from Theorem 3. Tipler 1977 (refs [7,8]), whose earlier result Theorem 3 extends, is NAMED-NOT-READ: known here only as Borde restates it ('with slightly stronger assumptions', the generic condition imposed on every geodesic, including those ending on the boundary).

published_statement: Abstract: 'Further, it is shown that in dimensions >= 3 causally compact topology-changing spacetimes cannot satisfy Einstein's equation (with a reasonable source); i.e., there are severe dynamical obstructions to topology change. This result extends a previous one due to Tipler. Like Tipler's result, it makes no assumptions about geodesic completeness; i.e., it does not permit topology change even at the price of singularities (of the standard incomplete-geodesic variety).' Sec. V, Theorem 3: 'Let M be a (time-oriented) causally compact interpolating spacetime of dimension >= 3 with initial surface S1 and final surface S2. Suppose that i) every full (i.e., no endpoint on S1 or on S2) null geodesic has a point on it at which F_abcd = U_[a R_b]ef[c U_d] U^e U^f != 0, where U^a is the tangent to the geodesic; and ii) for any point u0 on a past-complete, affinely parametrized null geodesic lambda(u), the half-integral null convergence condition (explained below) holds along lambda to the past of u0. Then M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1], and S1 and S2 are connected.' V.B: '(ii) holds along lambda to the past of u0 if for any delta > 0, there is b > 0 such that for any u1 < u0 there is an interval I of length >= b, with u1 > sup I and with INT_u^u0 R_ab U^a U^b du >= -delta for all u in I.' V: 'with certain restrictions on the curvature (which mainly follow from reasonable restrictions on the source)'. VI: any T_ab with T_ab V^a V^b >= K for all unit timelike V, K possibly negative (WEC is K = 0), gives R_ab U^a U^b >= 0 and so (ii). For quantum fields, integral conditions 'might perhaps hold. This is so far only a piece of wishful thinking.' IX.B: 'Another possibility is ... that there might be violations of the energy conditions large enough to allow assumption (ii) to be violated. Some discussions of wormhole creation are, for example, based precisely on large violations of the energy condition'. Weakening the curvature constraints 'would not affect the presence of causality violations, but it might permit topology change as a dynamical process.'
published_hypotheses: H1 smooth (C^1 vector field, smooth metric), non-degenerate Lorentz metric on a smooth, Hausdorff, paracompact manifold (Sec. II; Sec. VIII and IX.C name C^0 and degenerate metrics as outside)
H2 time-oriented (Theorem 3 statement; Sec. VII treats the non-time-orientable case separately)
H3 M is a connected interpolating spacetime between disjoint spacelike S1 (initial) and S2 (final). The boundary may carry a compact timelike tube T with T diffeomorphic to dS1 x [0,1] (Sec. II.A)
H4 causally compact: the closure of I(p) is compact for every p in M (Sec. III.B)
H5 dimension n >= 3 (the focusing lemma is stated for n > 2)
H6 (i) null generic condition on every FULL null geodesic, i.e. F_abcd != 0 somewhere. This is weaker than Tipler's version, which also covers geodesics ending on the boundary
H7 (ii) half-integral null convergence condition along every past-complete affinely parametrised null geodesic, to the past of every point on it

H8 (not a hypothesis of the theorem, only of its reading) Einstein's equation, with Lambda allowed, is used only to turn a restriction on T_ab into (i)/(ii). 'Reasonable source' means a T_ab for which (i) and (ii) hold. The theorem itself is purely a statement about curvature
No geodesic-completeness assumption (Lemma A supplies completeness of the horizon generators)
hypothesis_drift: NONE in the quotation. create.py:204-206 BORDE_DYNAMICS, create.py:73-75 and create.py:343-344 reproduce the abstract verbatim, with '>=' for the symbol (rederive D1). index3.py:884 paraphrases it ('in d >= 3 ... with a reasonable source') without change of content. The abstract's own gloss of the sentence ('makes no assumptions about geodesic completeness', which is Theorem 3's property) supports index3.py:884's placing it under SINGULARITY-NO-ESCAPE.

UNDETERMINED IN THE TREE, DETERMINED AT SOURCE: 'reasonable source'. canonical.json's hypothesis list and specthm.py:1149-1151 (R10 (e)) leave open 'whether reasonable excludes the source a throat needs'. The source defines it: 'reasonable' is a source restriction from which (i) and (ii) follow via Einstein's equation (Sec. V; VI: any T_ab bounded below on timelike vectors; IX.B names its violation). Computed here (rederive D6): for EVERY static zero-redshift throat, INT_{-oo}^{throat} R_kk du = -2 INT (r'/r)^2 < 0 along the radial null geodesic. For the Ellis throat the integral is -pi/(2 b0) to the throat and -pi/b0 over the whole line, and assumption (ii) FAILS at u0 = throat with delta = (pi+2)/(8 b0). So a static throat's source is outside Borde's 'reasonable' class. For creation, the contrapositive of Theorem 3 (z3 D7: unsat) gives the same: a smooth, time-oriented, causally compact, n >= 3 topology change must violate (i) or (ii). The Ellis case is an example family, not a general theorem about every throat. Throats with redshift function Phi != 0 were not computed here.

WEAKENED (the conclusion) at create.py:204-206: the tree carries 'cannot satisfy Einstein's equation'. The theorem concludes more ('M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1], and S1 and S2 are connected', D1), so disconnected initial or final surfaces are excluded even without topology change. It is also stated for any theory whose curvature satisfies (i) and (ii), not only for GR. Both make the tree's reading narrower than the source, which is not against the tree.

WEAKENED (the escape from THIS result) at create.py:84-86, create.py:216-218 (ESCAPES row 2 'weaken the curvature constraints' -> 'requires altering Einstein's equation'), index3.py:885 and specthm.py:1781-1783 (BORDE-ESCAPES counts len(create.ESCAPES)). IX.B names two sub-routes. One is altering Einstein's equation, 'fairly severe'. The other is energy-condition violation 'large enough to allow assumption (ii) to be violated', which stays within Einstein's equation, and Borde ties it explicitly to wormhole creation. The tree records only the first. The second defeats Theorem 3 only: Borde says it 'would not affect the presence of causality violations', so Theorem 1's CTC price stands (sibling audits gr-qc_9406053.json and gr-qc_9406053_escapes.json record the same omission).

SCOPE, juxtaposition only, at create.py:291-294 and create.py:343-346: the printed line 'and dynamically: <BORDE_DYNAMICS>' and the summary sentence come directly before 'THIS ONE DOES NOT CARE WHAT THE SOURCE IS'. That sentence is exact for the kinematic wall (Theorem 1; create.py:186 ties EXOTIC_MATTER_HELPS_CREATION to 'the line above'). It is not true of the dynamical result, whose hypotheses (i)-(ii) are exactly a restriction on the source. A reader of the printout can take the second sentence to cover the first. This is recorded, not repaired, and it changes no boolean the tree computes.

D1: md5 of the cached source; BORDE_DYNAMICS is verbatim in the abstract; Theorem 3's text, including the conclusion 'S1 and S2 are connected', the IX.B energy-violation sub-route and the VI 'wishful thinking' sentence are all present. D2: R_UU = k T_UU with Lambda for n = 3..6. D3: Sec. VI lemma (T(V,V) >= K for all unit timelike V implies T(U,U) >= 0), the boost limit, and T = C g as Borde's example. D4: the n = 3 null-direction claim, a quartic with leading coefficient R_MM/4, cubic when R_MM = 0, so at most 4 directions. D5: focusing blow-up at u* = -(n-2)/theta0, with coefficient 1/(n-2) undefined at n = 2. D6: zero-redshift throat R_kk = -2 r''/r; the identity INT R_kk = -2[r'/r] - 2 INT (r'/r)^2; Ellis R_kk = -2 b0^2/(b0^2+l^2)^2, whole-line -pi/b0, half-line to the throat -pi/(2 b0), INT_{-b0}^0 = -(pi+2)/(4 b0), R_kk < 0 everywhere, so (ii) fails at u0 = throat. D7 (z3): with 'reasonable' defined as implying (i) and (ii), 'cc & n>=3 & Einstein & reasonable & smooth & time-oriented -> no topology change' is proved (unsat), 'cc & n>=3 & Einstein -> no topology change' is NOT (sat), the contrapositive 'topology change -> not (i) or not (ii)' is proved, and dropping time-orientation or smoothness leaves the theorem silent (sat, sat). later_literature.what: An explicit nucleation of a throat in a Hawking-Borde compact-tube setup with a non-degenerate metric. That is Theorem 3's contrapositive seen in the tree's own case: creation happens only with a source outside the 'reasonable' class, and with CTCs (Theorem 1).

later_literature.what: A traversable throat in an asymptotically flat, globally hyperbolic spacetime requires ANEC violation. The literature's repair uses a half-line or modified ANEC (Galloway-Schleich-Witt-Woolgar gr-qc/9902061), close in form to Borde's (ii). This supports, for a different class, D6's finding that a throat's source violates integrated null convergence.

later_literature.what: As restated in the sibling audit, half-achronal ANEC fails for quantum fields in flat space (Dirichlet plate), so half-line integrated conditions are not generally obeyed by quantum sources. That bears on Borde's own caution that (ii) for quantum fields is 'wishful thinking'. Caution: Borde's (ii) ('comes repeatedly close to zero' in the past) is not the same condition as half-achronal ANEC, and whether quantum fields violate (ii) itself is not established here.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. Theorem 3 uses no measured datum, so no later measurement can move it. The only physical constant it touches, Lambda (unmeasured in 1994, measured since 1998 and in Planck 2018), drops out identically (D2). What Borde lacked, on his own account, was knowledge of how quantum sources behave on average: he calls the hope that quantum fields obey integral conditions like (ii) 'so far only a piece of wishful thinking' and says 'a lot more remains to be done'. Later work bears on it in both directions. (a) Classical and explicit constructions show that creating or holding a throat needs a source violating integrated null convergence: D6 for every static zero-redshift throat, 2505.02210 for an explicit nucleation, FSW for topological censorship. That CONFIRMS the theorem's logic: no counterexample satisfying (i)-(ii) exists, and the escapes all sit where Borde put them. (b) Later quantum-inequality work (read here only via restatement) indicates half-line integrated conditions can fail for quantum fields. That would mean (ii) is not guaranteed for semiclassical sources. It does not falsify Theorem 3, whose hypotheses would simply be unmet. It narrows how often the theorem APPLIES to a quantum source. It was not established here that (ii) itself fails for any quantum state. Evidence either way: no lacked datum makes the theorem wrong. The missing knowledge concerns whether real sources meet its hypothesis, and that question remains open. Not in M's favour either: even where (ii) fails, Borde (IX.B) and Theorem 1 keep the CTC price under causal compactness.
grade_evidence: The source STANDS as published. The tree's quotation is verbatim (D1), and every finite or closed-form step re-derives: Lambda-independence (D2), the Sec. VI energy lemma (D3), the n = 3 quartic (D4) and n > 2 focusing (D5). No datum enters, and the one constant it could touch (Lambda) drops out identically (D2). The TREE's USE holds on a smaller class than it states, at named sites. (1) Hypotheses the theorem needs are absent from the tree's statement: time-orientation and a smooth non-degenerate metric (create.py:204-206, 73-75, 343-344; specthm.py:1149-1151). z3 D7 shows the theorem is silent without either, and later work (Garcia-Heveling; Dowker-Surya) uses the degenerate-metric gap. (2) 'Reasonable source', which the tree leaves undetermined (specthm R10 (e)), is determined at source as the restriction yielding (i) and (ii). A static throat's source is computed to violate (ii) (D6), and the z3 contrapositive shows any causally compact n >= 3 creation must violate (i) or (ii). So the result's force against creation is exactly as strong as the claim that the source is 'reasonable', and create.py's ESCAPES row 2 (create.py:216-218, 84-86) drops the within-GR energy-violation escape Borde names for wormhole creation (IX.B). Not WRONG: nothing Borde states is contradicted, and no source satisfying (i)-(ii) with topology change is exhibited. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no moved datum moves it (D2). Not STANDS: the tree drops H1 and H2 and misreports IX.B's escape from this very result. Not in M's favour: removing Theorem 3 by an 'unreasonable' source leaves Theorem 1's CTC under causal compactness (IX.B, verbatim D1), and 2505.02210 shows exactly that price in an explicit nucleation.
what_would_change_the_grade: STANDS: the tree states H1 (smooth non-degenerate metric) and H2 (time-orientation) with the quotation, defines 'reasonable' as Borde's (i)-(ii), and records IX.B's energy-violation sub-route in create.ESCAPES. WRONG (of the source): an explicit smooth, time-oriented, causally compact n >= 3 topology-changing spacetime satisfying (i) and (ii). None is known here, and 2505.02210's construction violates all energy conditions. DATA-DEPENDENT: none possible, since the theorem has no numerical input.
